_: Region sheet for imperial-penal-south (2.5a1b). Talk is seeded from the region's published place records; every trait cites a lore dossier or says inferred.

norms.text: Debt is recorded and inherited; the Owing is the law where no court is.
The Rose is a ruin lived in by prison-born families who resent the word prison.
The dead are released to their families for a fee. The fee is recorded.
Procedure is recited even when it is monstrous. The reciter is often a decent person.

taboos.text: Burning a ledger in front of its keeper; it is how feuds start.

values.text: Possession as title: who holds the island holds the city.

contempts.text: Debt-brokers who buy an Owing and sell the person with it.
Outsiders who assume Blackrose city runs the Rose.

place.text: The south swallows people; you come in on a list and leave on another.

work.text: Work is transit, tolls and whatever comes out of the Rose.

people.text: Every neighbour owes a balance; ask to whom before trusting.

faction.text: The Chainbreakers audit the Owing and burn what they can prove false.

hist.text: Argonians who die in the Rose must reach the dirt near a tree.

empire.text: The Empire built the prison and abandoned the lists.

trade.text: Three rivers meet at Blackrose; everything moving south pays there.

danger.text: Umbriel's dead still walk the Rose's lower levels.

rumour.text: A bone-tag came back for a woman seen alive at the ford.

directions.text: Ways are given by the old cordon names: Prison road, Holding Fields, the Windlass.

addressTerms.text: Officials address people by status: debtor, holder, transferee.
Rose-born people call each other by family and generation.

neverSaid.text: A family's balance, aloud, in front of others.
Who carried the dead out after Umbriel.

grievances.text: The bone fee is the most resented payment in the south. The Chainbreakers pay it and record every payment.
The sealing note on the Vault door names the contents. It gives no name for whoever ordered them fed.

rumours.text: The Chainbreakers have found a false Owing with a living name on it.
Offerings left at the Sealed Vault are gone by the next visit.

views.text: Gideon keeps better records and asks fewer questions about ours.
Lilmoth's merchants buy what comes down the rivers without asking its origin.
The Naga-Kur country lies past the Rose. Travellers go round it.
The interior takes our dead and sends back nothing.
